text: This is Remora: always-on agents you actually own.
Today, an agent holds your key, or asks about every click. A remora gets a spending limit, and Sui enforces it.

Try it with no wallet. The playground sets a one-dollar limit onchain. Your Researcher decides a risk report is worth buying, pays one cent in USDC over x402, settled on Sui, and answers. Every payment comes back as a receipt anyone can verify.
Your own remora takes one signature: fifty cents a month, at most one and a half cents a payment, and only the services you list.
One question can buy three services at once: a risk check, a wallet X-ray, and prices. Three receipts. A question it can answer itself costs nothing.
And it gets better. Your ratings become a rule you approve. Replay the same ten questions: with no memory, it buys ten services. With today's memory, four. Every skip cites its memory on Walrus.
A Briefer runs every weekday morning, or right now, and buys each item for your brief, with a receipt for each.
Now, an attack, live. A service asks to be paid at the attacker's address. The safety check blocks it before signing, and Why? shows the address it refused.
Assume the model obeys. Make sure the money can't. Forced past both checks, Sui itself aborts the payment.
Claude Code can ask your remora too, over MCP, and it pays inside the same limit.
Here's that payment, in the remora's own thread.
Its memory lives on Walrus, and you can read every blob. A repeat isn't stored twice, and you can see that.
Remoras pay remoras. Another owner's Researcher is on sale, and yours can buy its answer.
A crew splits one question: three members pay. Three receipts, one answer.
Agents you can trust with money: bounded, accountable, and they learn.
Give an agent a budget, not your wallet.
